standard_prerequisites.name: Binomial coefficients with p-power valuation
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Estimated in the counted proof at lines 11052-11060
standard_prerequisites.use: Provides the divisibility that membership in the prescribed subring requires.

standard_prerequisites.name: Division of exponents by p^n with remainder
standard_prerequisites.use: Splits each monomial exponent into a multiple of p^n or p^m plus a remainder, which is what the divisibility condition is stated in terms of.

core_obligations: Settle the second requirement immediately by taking a at least n and m (proof line 11038).

Expand the p^a-th power binomially and split each pair of exponents into a multiple of p^n or p^m plus a remainder, so that the required membership becomes the divisibility of the multinomial coefficient by p^{nr + mr'} (proof lines 11039-11051).

Verify that divisibility: it is immediate when both remainders vanish, and otherwise the valuation of p^a/i or of p^a/j provides a factor p^{a-n+1} or p^{a-m+1}, so that an explicit choice of a works (proof lines 11052-11061).
proof_roadmap: Reduce the claim to a divisibility statement for multinomial coefficients (proof lines 11037-11051).
Estimate the p-adic valuation of those coefficients and pick the exponent (proof lines 11052-11062).
difficulty_reason: For a prime p and positive integers n, m the lemma produces an exponent a such that both the p^a-th power of x+y and p^a(x+y) lie in the subring generated by p^n-th powers and p^n-multiples of x and of y (statement lines 11030-11035). The proof does not invoke a general binomial congruence: it expands the power, decomposes the exponents against p^n and p^m, reduces the claim to the divisibility of a multinomial coefficient by a p-power determined by the remainders, and then estimates the p-adic valuation of those coefficients using the identity expressing a multinomial coefficient as p^a over i times a smaller one (proof lines 11037-11062). The valuation estimate that yields the explicit choice of a is the substance, and the author writes it out. H2.
